B.reason: wonokwo 'man', in MYS (e.g. 6.978) through logographic spellings read by metre; listed in ONCOJ.
tuka 'handful, bundle'; also the old unit for a bundle of rice; a close near-synonym of sheaf.
pige 'beard, whiskers'; the ordinary Japanese word that covers fish barbels.
mure 'flock, crowd' (noun and verb mure-), also mura.
worochi 'great serpent', written phonetically in the Kojiki (Yamata no worochi).
Not Old Japanese: uroko first appears in late Middle Japanese (15th-16th c.), replacing iroko and irokuzu.
tudumi, Kojiki song; a loan from Sanskrit dundubhi has been proposed but is not established.
meguri- 'go round', a near-synonym of turn.
kak- 'scratch, rake', used for stirring the brine in the Kojiki creation episode.
No Old Japanese attestation: first recorded in the Wamyosho (c. 934) as the colloquial form of irokuzu; reading the Kojiki's characters for 'fish scales' as iroko is a later editors' reading.
